text.en:
Directing the Formulation of the Philippine Carbon Market Policy
Framework. The DEN shall formulate, subject to the approval of the Inter-Agency
Committee on Carbon Markets (IACCM) created herein, the Philippine Carbon Market
Policy Framework, which shall serve as the primary national policy framework for the
Philippines' participation in carbon markets, including cooperative approaches under

of the Paris Agreement and voluntary carbon markets (VCM).
The Framework shall provide for, as a minimum, the following:
2

a. The Philippines' participation under Article 6 of the Paris Agreement,
i. guiding integrity principles governing carbon market participation;
il. eligibility requirements and authorization criteria applicable to mitigation
activities and entities seeking authorization for the international transfer of
mitigation outcomes;
ili. the mitigation activity development cycle, including the issuance of a no
objection letter, authorization of mitigation activity, issuance of mitigation
outcomes, authorization of mitigation outcomes, and first transfer phases;
iv. conditions applicable to the application of corresponding adiustments by
the Philippines;
v. benefit sharing mechanisms and guidelines; and
vi. the operation of the Philippine National Carbon Registry in tracking and
reporting internationally transferred mitigation outcomes;
b. The Philippines' participation in the VCM, including:
i. the eligibility requirements and general safeguards applicable to mitigation
activities and entities not seeking authorization under Article 6 of the Paris
i. the recognized carbon crediting standards and associated methodologies
applicable to voluntary activities;
Ill. benefit sharing mechanisms and guidelines; and
iv. oversight and reporting requirements applicable to CM activities under
the non-Article 6 track;
c. The principles governing fees and cost-recovery applicable to mitigation
activities under the Framework, including the categories of administrative
fees, the specific fee levels, methodologies, and procedures to be prescribed
in the rules and regulations through an Operations Manual to be issued by the
Designated National Authority (DNA) in accordance with prevailing laws,
rules, and regulations;
d. The institutional arrangements and roles of the DNA, line agencies, and other
relevant government entities in the implementation of the Framework; and
e. Guidance for other types of carbon credits or similar instruments, including,
but not limited to, transition credits. Any policy relating to fiscal and revenue
generation, carbon pricing, or the possible transition of the VCM to a
compliance carbon market, shall be subject to the concurrence of the
Department of Finance (DOF).
Section 2. Creation of the Inter-Agency Committee on Carbon Markets. To
ensure a whole-of-government approach and coherent policy direction in the
implementation of this Order, the IACCM is hereby established to be composed of the
heads of the following agencies:
3

Department of Energy (DOE
Department of Agriculture (DA)
Department of Transportation (DOT)
Department of Trade and Industry
Securities and Exchange Commission
The CCC shall serve as the Secretariat of the IACCM and provide the necessarv
technical and administrative support.
The members of the IACCM may designate their respective alternates, with
ranks not lower than Assistant Secretary or its equivalent, who shall be fully authorized
to decide for or on their behalf.
The lACCM may invite other departments, agencies, and relevant stakeholders
to participate in its meetings as observers, resource speakers, or technical advisers.
Section 3. Duties and Functions of the IACCM. The IACCM shall exercise
strategic policy oversight and inter-agency coordination on carbon market governance
under this Order and shall exercise the following duties and functions:
a. Ensure effective inter-agency coordination to promote alignment of carbon
market initiatives under this Order with the Philippines' NDCs, the national
greenhouse gas inventory, and the Enhanced Transparency Framework
under the Paris Agreement, and integrate carbon market outcomes into
national, sectoral, and local climate change plans;
b. Issue policy guidelines and provide strategic direction for the implementation
of the Framework, and ensure its consistent application across concerned
government agencies and sectors;
c. Periodically assess the implementation and effectiveness of the Framework
and recommend such policy measures, amendments, or updates as may be
necessary to strengthen its relevance, integrity, and alignment with national
climate objectives and evolving international developments;
d. Serve as the principal forum for inter-agency consultation, coordination, and
consensus-building on matters relating to carbon markets and carbon
crediting mechanisms, including issues elevated by the DNA, and facilitate
the development of common positions, policy approaches, and best practices
to support the effective implementation of the Framework;
e. Determine and approve the reasonable processing fees to be imposed for
applications and/or certifications necessary for or related to carbon markets;
f. Create such technical working groups, as may be necessary, and invite the
private sector, academe and scientific community, non-governmental
organizations/civil society organizations, or relevant stakeholders to assist in
the attainment of the objectives of this Order; and

g. Perform such other functions as may be necessary or incidental to its
purpose, or as may be directed by the President or the Executive Secretary.
Section 4. Designation of the DEN as the DNA. The DENR is hereby
designated as the DNA for carbon markets in the Philippines, including international
carbon markets under Article 6 of the Paris Agreement, the VCM, and such other
carbon market mechanisms as may hereafter be established.
The DEN shall ensure that the participation of the Philippines in the
international carbon markets under Article 6 of the Paris Agreement is consistent with
the national climate change policies and programs and other international
commitments.
Section 5. Role, Duties, and Functions of the DNA. The DENR, as the DNA,
shall exercise the following duties and functions:
a. Serve as the national authority for carbon markets in the Philippines,
including the country's participation in international carbon markets under
Article 6 of the Paris Agreement, the VCM, and such other carbon market
mechanisms that may be established;
b. Authorize or approve the registration and implementation of carbon
mitigation projects;
c. Establish, manage, and maintain the Philippine National Carbon Registry as
a centralized and transparent digital database for the tracking, recording,
issuance, authorization, transfer, cancellation, and retirement of carbon
credits and ITMOs;
d. Authorize the imposition of fees and charges as may be allowed under
prevailing laws and policies; and
e. Perform any other function as may be necessary or incidental to effectively
carry out its mandate as the DNA and to achieve the objectives of this Order.
Section 6. Roles of Line Agencies. The concerned government agencies,
offices, and instrumentalities shall participate in the operationalization and
implementation of the Framework by providing technical, policy, regulatory, and
sector-specific inputs consistent with their respective mandates, including, but not
limited to the following:
a. DENR, for nature-based solutions, forestry, and the waste sector;
b. DOE, for the energy sector;
c. DA and the Philippine Statistics Authority, for the agricultural sector;
d. DOTr, for transport-related carbon credit projects; and
e. DOF, for matters relating to fiscal policy, investment promotion, climate
finance, and the fiscal implications of carbon market transactions.

Issuance of the Philippine Carbon Market Policy Framework.
Within thirty (30) days from the effectivity of this Order, the DEN, as the DNA, is
hereby directed to draft and submit the Framework to the IACCM for review and
5

approval. The IACCM shall approve the Framework within thirty (30) days from receipt
of the submission, in accordance with existing laws, rules, and regulations.

Transitory Provision. Existing carbon crediting projects across all
sectors shall transition to the Philippine National Carbon Registry once the same
becomes operational. To facilitate such transition, all national government agencies and
instrumentalities maintaining records, databases, registries, or other information relating
to carbon crediting projects, including records and databases pertaining to the Clean
Development Mechanism, shall, within three (3) months from the effectivity of this
Order, share, transfer, or otherwise make available such data and information to the
DNA, subject to applicable laws, rules, and regulations.

Funding. The funding requirements for the initial implementation of
this Order shall be charged against the current appropriations of the DEN and other
concerned agencies and instrumentalities, subject to applicable government accounting
and auditing laws, rules, and regulations. Thereafter, the funding requirements for the
continued implementation of this Order shall be included in the budget proposal of the
DENR and other concerned agencies and instrumentalities, subject to the usual budget
preparation process and consistent with government accounting and auditing laws,
rules, and regulations.

Separability. If any section or part of this Order is declared
unconstitutional or invalid, the other sections or provisions not otherwise affected shall
remain in full force and effect.

Repeal. All issuances, orders, rules, and regulations, or parts
thereof that are inconsistent with the provisions of this Order are hereby repealed or
modified accordingly.

Effectivity. This Order shall take effect immediately upon its
publication in the Official Gazette or in a newspaper of general circulation.
DONE, in the City of Manila, this 13th day of October
of our Lord, Two Thousand and Twenty-Six.
By the President:
V RALPH G RESTO
Acting Exegutive Secretary
